newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee edges up against forward, spot dollar.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee edges up against forward, spot dollar.

text.p: The Indian rupee edged up against the forward and spot dollar in late morning trade on Thursday, dealers said.
November dollars opened higher at 0.86/0.88 rupees but fell to 0.82/0.85 as several banks showed interest in receiving premiums and selling forward dollars, they said.
"There is good receiving interest," said a dealer.
The Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) was in the market for October/November dollars, a bank dealer said.
Dealers said expectation of call money rates easing in the coming days also influenced the sentiment.
Overnight rates spurted to 7.0-7.5 percent on Thursday largely because of outflows from the banking system following Wednesday's successful three-year 30 billion rupee bond auction.
Call rates are expected to ease to around 6.0 percent.
The spot rupee gained to 35.802/812 in latest trade after opening the day at 35.815/825 as month-end demand for dollars seemed to be over, dealers said.
